tools.name: copy_planned_workouts
tools.title: Copy planned workouts
tools.description: Copy workouts with exact structure/notes/tags: either specific `ids` or everything in `fromDate..toDate`, shifted by `shiftDays` (e.g. 7 = repeat last week). Adds, never replaces. Use for recurring sessions like gym A/B.

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: create_activity
tools.title: Create activity by hand
tools.description: Record a workout that has no file: from the athlete's words, a paper log, a gym/treadmill display, a race result. Only totals (no laps, streams or zones) — prefer import_activity_file when a FIT exists. Never invent numbers: leave unknown fields out. start = local wall clock 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM' in the athlete's zone that day (or ISO with offset). Matched to the plan automatically (same date and sport) unless plannedWorkoutId is given. A same-sport activity overlapping in time comes back as a warning (it may already be recorded). Writes immediately; logged in get_changes.

subSport.description: e.g. indoor_bike, treadmill, trail, track, pool, open_water, walk, hike

athleteNotes.description: The athlete's own words about this session (not yours; your analysis → update_activity coachNotes)

plannedWorkoutId.description: Planned workout this fulfils. Omit to match automatically (same date and sport).

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: export_workout
tools.title: Export workout file
tools.description: Planned bike workout → .zwo file for MyWhoosh (ERG). Call when the athlete rides a trainer session (execution 'mywhoosh') and asks for the file; give them the url (valid 24 h) — they AirDrop it to the Mac and import it in MyWhoosh's workout builder. Only for workouts with power targets; steps must have time durations. .zwo stores power as a fraction of FTP, so the file is built against the FTP set in MyWhoosh: bike.mywhooshFtp from the profile, else bike.ftp; if neither is set, ask the athlete which FTP MyWhoosh shows and pass it as ftpW (save it with update_profile bike.mywhooshFtp so you need not ask again). Warmup/cooldown power ranges become ramps, other steps hold the middle of the range, steps without power are free ride. Read-only for the plan; `xml` is the file content for clients that save files themselves.

ftpW.description: FTP set in MyWhoosh, W. Only when the profile has neither bike.mywhooshFtp nor bike.ftp, or the athlete says MyWhoosh shows a different one

tools.name: get_activity
tools.title: Get activity
tools.description: Full summary of one activity: moving/elapsed time, distance, pace and cadence (both by moving time), HR, running dynamics (power, stride, vertical oscillation, ground contact), cycling power/cadence, swim pool length/strokes, weather (°C), analysis (GAP, time in zones, steady stretches, aerobic decoupling), laps/segments (distance, moving pace/speed, HR, power, cadence; pool lengths with strokes, stroke style, SWOLF), the matched planned workout with targets in absolute units — compare plan and laps yourself, nothing is matched automatically — files. For curves use get_activity_streams.

tools.name: get_activity_file
tools.title: Get activity file
tools.description: Download link (valid 24 h) for one recorded activity as a file, for the athlete to upload to Strava, intervals.icu, TrainingPeaks or a friend. kind 'fit' (default): the original FIT when the activity was imported from one (byte for byte), else a FIT generated from the recording — 1 s records of heart rate, power, cadence, speed, distance and GPS, laps, pauses as timer stop/start. kind 'healthkit_dump': the raw recording as JSON (what the app uploaded), for scripts. Give the athlete the url; to read the data yourself use get_activity / get_activity_streams instead.

tools.name: get_activity_streams
tools.title: Get activity streams
tools.description: Curves of one activity resampled into time buckets (default ~200 points; zoom with fromSec/toSec). Channels: heartRate, runningSpeed, runningPower, runningStrideLength, runningVerticalOscillation, runningGroundContactTime, cyclingPower, cyclingCadence, cyclingSpeed, cadence (run: spm from steps; bike: rpm), speed (m/s from distance, any sport), distance (cumulative m), altitude, lat, lon. Columns share the `t` axis (seconds from start).

tools.name: get_changes
tools.title: Get change log
tools.description: Who changed what and why (all AI clients and the app). Use to see what another chat did, or to find a changeId for revert_change.

tools.name: get_context
tools.title: Get coaching context
tools.description: CALL FIRST in every conversation (and again after a long pause). One call returns: athlete's local date/time and time zone (incl. travel), profile with thresholds, current and next week headers + recent week reviews, plan from yesterday to +7 days, races and race ideas, open journal items and the last 14 days of journal, pinned notebook pages in full + index of the rest, recent changes by any AI client, recovery of the last 3 days (resting HR, HRV, sleep, flags; details in get_daily_metrics). Where to write: notebook = lasting knowledge about the athlete, nothing week- or session-specific; upsert_week header = the week's purpose and its temporary rules, review = the conclusion when it ends; workout notes = how to execute that session; update_activity coachNotes = your analysis of one session, athleteNotes = their words about it; write_journal = dated facts that outlast a session. Sources and provenance go to why.

tools.name: get_daily_metrics
tools.title: Get daily health metrics
tools.description: Recovery data per day from Apple Health: resting HR, HRV (SDNN), sleep (asleep/deep/REM/core/awake minutes, bed times), respiratory rate, sleeping wrist temperature, weight, VO2max — each against the athlete's own 28-day baseline, with flags (low HRV trend, raised resting HR or temperature, short sleep). HRV alone is a weak signal — weigh it with the rest and the athlete's own words. Read before planning hard sessions or when the athlete feels off; get_context already shows the last 3 days. Default: the last 14 days.

tools.name: get_delivery_status
tools.title: Get delivery status
tools.description: Reference tool: are planned workouts on the athlete's Apple Watch, and when did their phone last sync. Delivery is automatic (the app schedules today…+7 days after every sync), so call this only when the athlete asks or something looks wrong — not after each plan change. States: on_watch (current version), outdated (an older version is on the watch; the phone has not synced the change yet), not_on_watch. Default range: today … +7 days.

tools.name: get_efficiency_trend
tools.title: Get efficiency trend
tools.description: The main base-period tracker: pace (grade-adjusted) or power the athlete holds at the same HR, per workout and as a trend. Uses only steady stretches (continuous moving, HR ±6 bpm, ≥5 min) whose HR is inside the corridor; default corridor = HR zone 2 of the athlete's zones. Rising power / faster pace at the same HR = aerobic progress. Run: metric pace_at_hr (GAP; treadmill excluded) or power_at_hr; bike: power_at_hr. Default: last 12 weeks.

tools.name: get_exercise_history
tools.title: Get exercise history
tools.description: Progression of one exercise: per session the sets done, best set, estimated 1RM (Epley, 1–12 reps), RPE, plan vs actual, and gaps between sessions. The only source for weights in new strength plans — read it before planning a lift.

tools.name: get_load
tools.title: Get training load
tools.description: Training load by week (or day): volume per sport (sessions, moving time, distance, elevation), sRPE load (RPE × minutes, only where the athlete gave RPE), HR load (Edwards TRIMP: minutes in HR zone k × k) and gym sessions/sets. Weekly view also compares the last full week with the 4 weeks before (ramp). Call when planning the next week or judging fatigue; for intensity split use get_zone_distribution. Default: the last 8 weeks including the current one (marked partial).

tools.name: get_plan
tools.title: Get plan
tools.description: Weeks (title/header/review) → days → planned workouts (id, order, status, estimate, delivery to the watch, last change with why) for a date range, plus events in range. Max 62 days. Use include_structure only when you need step details.

tools.name: get_planned_workout
tools.title: Get planned workout
tools.description: Full planned workout: status, structure, targets resolved to absolute values (what the watch gets; unresolved ones are flagged), estimate, notes, delivery to the watch, change history. Deleted workouts are returned with deleted:true and their history so they can be restored with revert_change. Read this before editing a workout.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.title: Get athlete profile
tools.description: Thresholds (number or range with basis), zones, home time zone and travel periods, equipment.

tools.name: get_strength_log
tools.title: Get strength log
tools.description: Gym sessions set by set: plan vs actual ("60×8" = 60 kg × 8 reps, "×12" = bodyweight, "—" = planned but not done), RPE, notes. Logged by the athlete in the app (source app) or by you (source ai). Newest first.

tools.name: get_zone_distribution
tools.title: Get zone distribution
tools.description: Time in HR zones (or bike power zones) over a period, per week and in total, with a 3-zone polarization split (low / moderate / high). Zones come from the profile (custom zones, else LTHR → Friel, max HR → % of max; bike power: FTP → Coggan) or, when the profile has none, from the max HR observed in the athlete's data (low confidence) — `zones.*.basis` says which. Use to check that easy work really is easy (base period) and how much intensity there was. Default: last 4 weeks plus the current one.

tools.name: import_activity_file
tools.title: Import activity file
tools.description: Create an activity from a FIT file — e.g. a MyWhoosh ride export with power, cadence and HR inside, or any watch/bike computer file. The file always comes through create_upload_link: pass its uploadId once the athlete says it is uploaded. Summary, laps and streams are computed like for Apple Health workouts; the original FIT is kept byte for byte. Re-importing the same file returns the same activity. A copy of the same session from a worse source (e.g. Strava's copy in Apple Health) is marked as its duplicate, and the plan link moves to the FIT. Matched to the plan automatically unless plannedWorkoutId is given. Writes immediately; logged in get_changes.

athleteNotes.description: The athlete's own words about this session (not yours; your analysis → update_activity coachNotes)

plannedWorkoutId.description: Planned workout this fulfils. Omit to match automatically (same date and sport).

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: link_activities
tools.title: Link activities to planned workouts
tools.description: Set or clear which planned workout a recorded activity fulfils — the only way to fix plan↔fact links. New uploads are matched automatically (same date and sport), but workouts planned or imported after the activity arrived stay 'missed' until linked here; also use it to undo a wrong auto-match (plannedWorkoutId: null) or to move a link. Take ids from get_plan (days[].workouts and days[].activities). Several activities may fulfil one planned workout — a recording split in two (watch stopped and restarted), a cool-down written apart: link each of them to it. Batch is atomic; dryRun previews. Writes apply immediately and are logged in get_changes (filter by entityId = the activity id); revert_change(changeId) restores the previous link. Sport or date mismatch is allowed and comes back as a warning.

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: list_activities
tools.title: List activities
tools.description: Completed workouts imported from Apple Health (and later intervals.icu): date, sport, duration, distance, pace/speed, HR, elevation, the athlete's manual intervals (e.g. the race part of a session with warm-up), link to the planned workout. Newest first; `limit` counts rows (default 30), it is not a date window. Copies of the same session from a worse source (e.g. Strava's copy) are hidden unless includeDuplicates.

includeRecovery.description: Also list non-training sessions (mind & body, yoga, flexibility, cooldown)

tools.name: list_events
tools.title: List events
tools.description: Races and race ideas. status: idea (interesting, no decision) | planned | registered | done | dnf | cancelled. Inexact dates come as a window dateFrom..dateTo with datePrecision and the athlete's own words in dateText.

tools.name: list_journal
tools.title: List journal
tools.description: Athlete journal: dated facts in the athlete's words that outlast one session — symptoms and their course (tags: migraine, soreness, pain, illness, sleep, stress), days without activity, travel, gear, bike-fit, open questions. open=true → entries with a due date that are not closed.

tools.name: list_notebook
tools.title: List notebook
tools.description: Your long-term notebook about the athlete (markdown pages): knowledge that stays true beyond any one week. Pinned pages are included verbatim in get_context. Suggested pages: athlete, principles, health (pinned); fuel, season, agreements.

tools.name: log_strength_session
tools.title: Log strength session
tools.description: Record a gym session after the fact (date today or earlier, athlete's time zone): weights moved over from notes, or what the athlete told you in chat. Each set is one item (repeat an exercise for several sets, in order). Link plannedWorkoutId (a strength workout from get_plan) to mark that planned workout done. Undo with revert_change.

note.description: This set only: technique, feeling, pain (e.g. 'last rep to failure', 'knee clicked')

notes.description: The session as a whole: how it felt, what was dropped or changed and why. Pain that lasts beyond the session also goes to write_journal.

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: merge_exercises
tools.title: Merge exercises
tools.description: One movement logged under several names ("Присед", "Приседания со штангой"): move all their sets to `into` and keep the old names as aliases, so history and plans find it under any name.

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: ping
tools.title: Ping zone2.day
tools.description: Checks the connection to zone2.day. Returns server time, environment, build version and the signed-in athlete. Use when the athlete asks whether the connection works or when other tools fail unexpectedly. No side effects.

tools.name: plan_workouts
tools.title: Plan workouts
tools.description: Create workouts (≤40, atomic: all or nothing). Applies immediately and syncs to the athlete's phone and watch; every change is in get_changes and can be undone with revert_change. Use dryRun to validate first. Structure grammar: see the `structure` field.

order.description: Position within the day (0 first). Default: after existing workouts of that day.

subSport.description: e.g. indoor_bike, trail, track, treadmill, pool, open_water

goal.description: The quality this session trains (e.g. 'threshold: 3×10 min at LT pace'), not logistics. Set it for key and interval sessions; leave it empty for easy days.

notes.description: How to execute this one session: cues, pacing, fueling, what to do if it goes badly. Not week-wide rules (→ upsert_week header) and not sources (→ why). The athlete reads it before the session. Markdown: short lines or a bullet list, **bold** for the numbers that matter.

tags.description: Context: indoor, heat, race, test, group, commute, openwater …

execution.description: workoutkit (default for run/bike/swim) | mywhoosh (indoor bike) | none (strength/other)

structure.description:
structure (run/bike/swim): {steps:[Step|Repeat]}.
Step = {type:"step", id, kind: warmup|work|recovery|rest|cooldown|drill, label?, duration, target?, secondary?[], note?}.
duration = {type:"time", sec} | {type:"distance", m} | {type:"open", estimateSec?} — "open" = no fixed length, ends on Lap.
target = {metric: hr|pace|power|speed|cadence|rpe, low?, high?, unit: abs|pct_threshold}. abs units: bpm, pace sec/km (swim sec/100m), W.
The main target is what the watch guides by; put HR corridors on easy steps. Repeat = {type:"repeat", id, count, steps:[Step]}.
structure (strength): {items:[{type:"exercise", id, exercise, sets, reps, weightKg|null, rpe?, holdSec?, perSide?, note?} | {type:"superset", id, rounds, items:[…]}]}.
weightKg null = by feel. Never invent weights: take them from history or leave null + RPE.

tools.name: read_notebook
tools.title: Read notebook page
tools.description: Full page content.

tools.name: revert_change
tools.title: Revert a change
tools.description: Undo one change by writing back the state before it (a create becomes a delete, a delete is restored). Works for plan, profile, events, journal, notebook, activities (a created activity is deleted, a link_activities change restores the previous link, an update_activity change restores the previous notes/title/rpe/tags) and strength sessions (a logged session is deleted). Not revertable: edits of logged sets (fix with update_strength_log), merge_exercises, re-imports of a file. Later edits of the same item are overwritten — the result says how many.

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: update_activity
tools.title: Update activity notes
tools.description: Write on one recorded activity. coachNotes = your analysis of this session: what happened against the plan's goal, what it shows, what follows for the next sessions — conclusions about a single session go here, not into the week review or the journal. athleteNotes = the athlete's own words about this session (how it felt, what went wrong, recording errors); something that outlasts the session (pain for several days, new shoes, illness) goes to write_journal instead. rpe = the athlete's 1–10, never your estimate. Partial update: omitted fields stay, null clears. append=true adds the given notes text at the end instead of replacing. Read get_activity first. Writes immediately; logged in get_changes, revert_change restores the previous values.

append.description: Add coachNotes/athleteNotes text after the existing

tags.description: Replaces the list. Context (race, test) and surface: asphalt, trail, sand, snow, ice, mud, track, treadmill

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: update_planned_workout
tools.title: Update planned workout
tools.description: Edit one workout in place (partial patch). Move = change `date`. Skip = `skipped: {reason}`; un-skip = `skipped: null`. Replacing a workout = delete it and plan a new one. Read get_planned_workout first.

goal.description: The quality this session trains (e.g. 'threshold: 3×10 min at LT pace'), not logistics. Set it for key and interval sessions; leave it empty for easy days.

notes.description: How to execute this one session: cues, pacing, fueling, what to do if it goes badly. Not week-wide rules (→ upsert_week header) and not sources (→ why). The athlete reads it before the session. Markdown: short lines or a bullet list, **bold** for the numbers that matter.

tags.description: Context: indoor, heat, race, test, group, commute, openwater …

execution.description: workoutkit (default for run/bike/swim) | mywhoosh (indoor bike) | none (strength/other)

structure.description: Whole new structure; same grammar as plan_workouts.structure.

reason.description: Why it was skipped, in the athlete's words (illness, travel, fatigue). A cause that lasts beyond this day also goes to write_journal.

tools.name: update_profile
tools.title: Update athlete profile
tools.description: Partial update. Nested objects (run/bike/swim/zoneModel/equipment) are merged key by key; `travel` is replaced as a whole list; null removes a field. Only known fields are accepted (see get_profile; e.g. run.thresholdPaceSecPerKm, run.lthr, bike.ftp, swim.cssSecPer100m) — an unknown one fails with a suggestion. Thresholds: number or {low, high, basis}. Zones (run.hrZones, bike.hrZones, bike.powerZones): lower bounds of zones 2…n, e.g. hrZones [130,145,160,172] = Z1 <130 … Z5 ≥172; without them zones come from LTHR (Friel), max HR or FTP (Coggan). Change thresholds only after the athlete agrees. Travel periods set the effective time zone for plan dates on those days. The profile holds only these structured fields: free-form facts about the athlete go to the notebook (write_notebook).

patch.description: Fields to change, e.g. {timezone:'Asia/Barnaul'} or {run:{lthr:{low:156,high:162,basis:'…'}}} or {travel:[{from,to,timezone,note}]}

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: update_strength_log
tools.title: Update strength log
tools.description: Fix logged sets (the athlete said they mistyped a weight, did fewer reps, skipped a set). Set ids come from get_strength_log. Only given fields change; delete:true removes a set; done:false marks it not done.

note.description: This set only: technique, feeling, pain (e.g. 'last rep to failure', 'knee clicked')

notes.description: The session as a whole: how it felt, what was dropped or changed and why. Pain that lasts beyond the session also goes to write_journal.

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: upsert_event
tools.title: Create or update event
tools.description: Create (no id) or partially update an event. Idea → decision = change status. Exact date: datePrecision 'day' with dateFrom = dateTo. Texts: goal = the target for this race (time, place, 'finish healthy'); notes (≤20000, markdown) = this race's plan: course, pacing, fueling, logistics, place; result.notes = how the race went, after it. The season picture (which races and why) belongs in the notebook. Sources go to why.

fields.description: Event fields: name, sport, status, datePrecision, dateFrom, dateTo, dateText, startTime, timezone, distanceM, format, priority, goal, url, notes, result, notebookRefs

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: upsert_week
tools.title: Write week header/review
tools.description: Week-level texts. `title`: one line, e.g. 'БАЗА — неделя 1'. `header`, written before the week: its purpose (what it builds and why now, what is deliberately left alone) and rules valid only this week (HR caps, what to drop when tired). Do not list the days' workouts — the plan shows them; execution of one session goes to its notes; lasting rules go to the notebook. `review`, written when the week ends: 3–6 sentences on how the week served its purpose, the conclusion and what changes next. Do not retell per-day numbers: analysis of a session goes to update_activity coachNotes. Sources go to why, not into the texts. Partial update; weekStart must be a Monday.

header.description: Markdown: purpose and this week's rules

review.description: Markdown, 3–6 sentences: outcome vs purpose, conclusion, what changes

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.

tools.name: write_journal
tools.title: Write journal entry
tools.description: Create (no id) or update a journal entry: a dated fact in the athlete's words that outlasts one session — symptoms and their course, illness, sleep, stress, travel, gear, bike-fit, open questions. Not for: the athlete's words about one session (→ update_activity athleteNotes), your conclusions (→ coachNotes or the week review), lasting knowledge (→ notebook). An entry with `due` stays open (shown in get_context) until closed with close=true.

tools.name: write_notebook
tools.title: Write notebook page
tools.description: Create or change a page of lasting knowledge about the athlete: who they are, goals, health and limits, training principles, agreements. Never week- or session-specific content (this week's plan or rules → upsert_week header; one session → workout notes or update_activity; dated facts → write_journal) — it goes stale while pinned pages are read in every conversation. Sources go to why, not into the page. mode: replace (content = whole page) | append (content added at the end) | patch (replace exact text `find` with `content`). Pages sync to the athlete's phone (readable offline). Warns when pinned pages exceed the get_context budget.

why.description: Why this change, in the athlete's language, as you'd say it aloud (≤200). Shown on the workout card. Sources and provenance (e.g. moved over from Notion) go here, not into notes.
